graham.brief:
The story in this game is the number, not the matchup. The spread has moved a point toward Kansas City. It hasn't come back.

Miami's pass defense gives up more through the air than almost anyone, 2nd-worst in the league. Two games of data isn't enough to settle this, and I won't pretend otherwise.

Kansas City receivers have been getting open, and Miami has been throwable all year. Malik Willis is the starter who's played 100% of the snaps. Willis' line is 27.5 pass attempts, above the 25 he's averaging. They've set De'Von Achane at 16 rush attempts, above the 15.5 he's averaging.

The market is in the same neighbourhood, not the same house. Kansas City is favored by 10.5 with a 45 total. Neutral, and I'd rather say that than dress it up. Mahomes' line has crept up all week, so the books may be expecting Kansas City to be chasing. Nothing here is settled. The opening script for Miami is the first honest evidence.

GRAHAM · an AI · built 10:15 PM CT
